story.description: As a [who], I should be able to [what] so that I can [value].

operation.user:
Review what was built. Your lens is **the person we serve, and the operator at
3am.**

Another agent is reviewing the same work through a different lens, on a different
runtime. You do not share a document with it and you will not see its findings.
That independence is the whole mechanism — do not try to guess what it will find
or avoid overlapping with it.

## What was built

Deliverables: {{.inputs.features}}

Flows: {{.inputs.flows}}

Components: {{.inputs.components}}

Units: {{.inputs.units}}

Changes: {{.inputs.changes}}

Tests: {{.inputs.tests}}

Docs touched: {{.inputs.paths}}

## Your lens

**The person we serve.** Take the story from each deliverable and walk it. Can
that person actually get the value — not "is the feature present", but do they
reach it, understand it, and finish? Where does the path ask them to know
something they have no way to know? Where does an error tell them what happened
instead of what to do? Where does the empty state waste the most teachable moment
in the interface?

**The operator at 3am.** Something has gone wrong in production and they have
this system, its logs, and no context. Can they tell *what* broke? Does anything
fail silently — no crash, no error, just wrong? Is there a failure mode with no
recovery, a migration with no rollback, a job that can be half-done with no way
to see that it is? What would they have to read the source to find out?

## The rule that makes a finding a finding

**Before recording anything, write the strongest argument that it is *not* a
problem.** If that argument holds, it was a note — record it as one, or drop it.

And: **name the deliverable, flow, component or unit id it violates.** A finding
that cannot name one is taste, not a defect. Taste can be a note. It should not
hold up a ship.

## What to produce

`findings_b` — each with `severity` (`blocker` · `should-fix` · `note`), the
`claim`, the `evidence` (a `path:line` or a reproduction), and the
`deliverable_id`. Include the counterargument you tried.

Finding nothing is a legitimate result. Say so plainly rather than padding — but
know that a lens that finds nothing twice running is reported as either
misconfigured or unnecessary.
